caption: The drawing depicts a single large cross with flared ends, centered on a plain, off-white background. The cross is rendered in shades of light brown and pink, and features a consistent geometric pattern of circular and semi-circular designs along its entire length, within the arms and shaft. At the intersection of the arms, there is a starburst-like motif. The edges of the cross are lined with evenly spaced, notched or serrated decorations. Attached to the top of the cross is a short, light brown string or cord, looped and trailing upwards. In the lower right corner of the image, there is a small hand-written text that reads: “MARJ. G. COFFIN - 1905 - N.M.”
title: Cedar Cross
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
